info.name: 318 E-Commerce - Full Manual Coverage (core flow + uncovered endpoints + negative/permission + failure branches)
info.description:
A superset of 318-ecommerce-e2e: covers U1-U5 / P1-P4 / O1-O6 / I1-I4 / PAY1-PAY4 / AI1-AI4, plus the 400/401/403/404/409/423 negative paths, the payment.failed branch and the low-stock alert open/resolve lifecycle.

Preconditions: all six services running, and order-service / inventory-Service / payment-service must run with the kafka profile (otherwise the steps marked [KAFKA] fail).

How to run: Run the whole collection in folder order 0 -> 6 (or Send request by request). Every {{...}} is a collection variable, so no Environment is needed.

Two places need a human:
1) resetToken in folder 5: the password-reset token is never returned over the API - open http://localhost:8081/h2-console (jdbc:h2:mem:userservicedb, user sa, empty password), run SELECT * FROM password_reset_token, paste the value into the collection variable resetToken and re-send 5.3.
2) folder 6 needs a real OPENAI_API_KEY, otherwise 6.1 fails (it is tolerated and will not be reported as a failure).

Repeatability: every run generates a new runTag which is embedded in product names and emails, so a full re-run never hits 409; stock, orders and payments do accumulate, though. Restart the services first if you want completely clean numbers.

Re-running a single folder breaks the ordering dependencies (e.g. folder 2 asserts stock 48 which depends on folder 1 having just run), so always run the whole collection.

I4 is maintained by a Kafka Streams topology: first check whether the consumer group exists - docker exec 318-kafka kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --list. If inventory-alerts is missing, the I4 topology is not running at all and no alert will ever be produced; if it exists, this is just the topology commit delay (30s by default) and re-sending the request later is enough'); }); return; }

Note that ai-customer-service disguises downstream failures as 401 - an LLM exception triggers Spring forwarding to /error, and that internal dispatch carries no identity (JwtAuthenticationFilter is a OncePerRequestFilter and skips ERROR dispatches), so the security chain answers 401. A 401 therefore does not mean the token is wrong; the real cause is in that service console stack trace. Common ones: the process never saw OPENAI_API_KEY (the log says 'Your api key: z is invalid'), or OPENAI_MODEL is not a valid model name.');
